newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says to be formally split up after June 1999.
newsitem.headline: NTT says to be formally split up after June 1999.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference on Wednesday that the firm would be formally split up after shareholders approve the move at a meeting scheduled for the end of June 1999.
But he added that although formal approval would come then, the firm hoped to start the process of separating the firm's business as soon as possible.
Miyazu said earlier this year he was considering moving forward NTT's restructuring schedule, originally set for 1999, to cope with rapid developments in global telecommunications markets.

"Our intention is to move as quickly as possible, but it looks as though it will be difficult to complete the restructuring business by next year's shareholders' meeting scheduled for June," Miyazu told a news conference.

He made the comment after what looked like tax and legal barriers to NTT's break-up were resolved on Tuesday and Wednesday, leading the way for a bill splitting NTT to be passed by parliament by the end of June.
The ruling Liberal Democratic Party decided on Wednesday to give preferential tax breaks to NTT when it splits into three companies under a holding-company structure.
The LDP also decided on Tuesday to lift a ban on holding companies as soon as next January.
Bills to remove the holding company ban and to split NTT will be submitted to parliament on March 11.
